purpose: Synthetic-only test of sending ffconcat CENC decryption options over stdin or an inherited pipe FD, with no key file and no raw key in FFmpeg argv
synthetic_input: Three-second 440 Hz, 44100 Hz mono FLAC in ordinary MP4 and fragmented MP4, encrypted locally using synthetic CENC AES-CTR key and KID; no real media or credentials
duration_directive: omitted; duration was detected from each MP4
implementation_implication: Send the ffconcat script through stdin or an inherited pipe FD and use a fully qualified child URL such as `file:/absolute/path` for local files (or an already-qualified https URL for remote media). A bare absolute filesystem path is resolved relative to `pipe:0` by this invocation and becomes an invalid `pipe:/...` URL. This avoids writing the key to disk and works for full decode plus both input-side and output-side one-second seeks without a duration directive. The probe does not validate real provider URLs, credentials, remote authorization, or device playback.

official_reference.title: FFmpeg Formats Documentation, concat demuxer syntax
official_reference.note: Documents per-file `option key value` and `duration` directives.
